sections.title: How does the Cat chocolate toxicity calculator work?
sections.html:
The Cat chocolate toxicity calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports chocolate type in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in your cat's weight, the methylxanthines dose and the total methylxanthines received.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Cat chocolate toxicity calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Chocolate type=methylxanthines dose × your cat's weight ÷ amount eaten
Chocolate type=total methylxanthines received ÷ amount eaten

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Take Your cat's weight = 10 kg, Chocolate type set to Milk chocolate, Amount eaten = 1000 g and Methylxanthines dose = 10 kg. The calculator returns Total methylxanthines received = 2260 mg.

The point of the example is the scale, not the particular digits: swap in your own figures and the same relationship produces your answer.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Total methylxanthines received = 2260 mg should be roughly the size you expected from Your cat's weight = 10 kg and Chocolate type set to Milk chocolate.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Mass, opening in grams
  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Mass, opening in milligrams

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Cat chocolate toxicity calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Putting a biological quantity into a scale you can picture
  • Comparing two organisms, populations or processes
  • Supporting a lesson, a lecture or a field note
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — your cat's weight, the methylxanthines dose and the total methylxanthines received — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

faq.q: What does the Cat chocolate toxicity calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns chocolate type, derived from your cat's weight, the methylxanthines dose and the total methylxanthines received. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Cat chocolate toxicity calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for your cat's weight, the methylxanthines dose and the total methylxanthines received, which is 3 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter your cat's weight in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Your cat's weight opens in kilograms and the chip beside it offers 29 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Total methylxanthines received = 2260 mg. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Cat chocolate toxicity calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
